coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: UCSF Illinois Street Garage
record.summary: 590 Illinois Street, a nine-story, 500-space parking garage the owner identified as the southernmost portion of what this project had tracked as one combined "block 34" fragment -- split off 2026-09-22 along a visible roofline seam from the Bayfront Medical Building immediately north of it (data/records/ucsf_bayfront_medical_building.json), both built under UCSF's own "Block 34 Clinical Building and Parking Garage" project.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL BUILDING, APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- a real, standing structure clearly visible in Esri satellite imagery (not open land). Boundary is the real-gap-fragment's own traced edge (following the street buffer's curb radius) with the north cap (and, for the garage, the cut from the building to its north) re-derived to the real street angle -- see digitization_method -- not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. The split between this building and its neighbor follows a visible satellite roofline seam, not a surveyed or permitted lot line -- treat the exact boundary as indicative, not authoritative.
notes.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) between 3rd St and Illinois St, south of 16th St, extended down to Mariposa St. The owner directly identified this whole real-gap fragment as capturing two separate real buildings, not one, and directed cutting it at the visible gap between the two rooflines in Esri satellite imagery (lat 37.76578) -- see mission_bay_block_33.geojson (now UCSF Valley Center for Vision -- west building) for the piece north of that cut.

milestones.text: Construction begins on the Illinois Street Garage portion of the Block 34 project specifically (500 spaces, nine levels), per Clark Construction's own press release: "Clark started construction on the garage portion of the development in April 2021" -- distinct from the clinical building's own Sept/Oct 2021 groundbreaking

open_questions: 2026-09-22, corroborating data point: this project's own DataSF business-registration spatial join (src/join_retail.py, out/retail_needs_review_approximate.csv), re-run after this record's geometry was added, shows a registration (Sentry Security Services, Inc.) whose point-location falls inside this record's polygon listing '590 Illinois St' as its address -- matching the 590 Illinois St address already sourced from UCSF Real Estate's own project page, not contradicting it. The join is spatial-only and never auto-confirmed per that script's own docstring, so this is logged as corroboration, not an independent primary source.

SPLIT 2026-09-22: this record was previously mission_bay_block_33 (a probable, geographically-inferred identity for the WHOLE of what is now UCSF Valley Center for Vision -- west building, data/records/ucsf_valley_center_for_vision_west.json -- a mistaken pairing). The owner directly corrected this: the garage is the southernmost piece of the former mission_bay_block_34 fragment, not block 33. This record's geometry is now the south piece of that split (see ucsf_bayfront_medical_building.geojson for the north piece); the split follows a visible satellite roofline seam, not a surveyed or permitted lot line, and its exact boundary should be treated as indicative rather than authoritative.
Cost of the garage alone (vs. the combined ~$335.8M clinical-building-plus-garage project figure reported elsewhere) was not found.

2026-09-21 pass: added an April 2021 construction-start milestone from UCSF Real Estate's own combined project page for 'Bayfront Medical Building and Illinois Street Garage.' This is a combined-project date covering both buildings, not a garage-specific one, though Clark Construction's own press release (see milestone above) does independently corroborate April 2021 as garage-specific.
